page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Optimized3.Flex.8-128 is a flexible compute instance powered by an Intel Xeon 6354 processor running at a base clock speed of 3.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The server allocates 8 dedicated physical cores mapped to 16 virtual CPUs with two hardware threads per core. System memory is provisioned at 128.0 GB of RAM, yielding an allocation ratio of 8.0 GB per virtual processor thread, or 16.0 GB per physical execution core. Dedicated hardware accelerators are omitted, with zero onboard graphics processing units present.

Storage architecture requires external networked block volumes, as the VM.Optimized3.Flex.8-128 does not include integrated local NVMe or solid-state storage. Each deployment includes one complimentary public IPv4 address for networking. Because CPU threads are backed by dedicated physical cores rather than shared or oversubscribed hypervisor resources, execution behavior avoids noisy-neighbor contention under continuous compute operations.

The 1:8 core-to-memory ratio provides a high memory density relative to standard balanced instances, positioning this configuration for memory-bound and thread-heavy tasks. Workloads that benefit from this profile include in-memory caching tiers, medium-scale relational databases, data transformation pipelines, continuous integration runners, and application serving environments requiring large working memory sets.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Optimized3.Flex.8-128 is an x86_64 server instance powered by an Intel Xeon 6354 processor operating at a 3.0 GHz base frequency. It features 8 dedicated physical processor cores presenting 16 virtual CPUs via simultaneous multithreading, coupled with 128.0 GB of system memory. This yields a dense 8.0 GB memory allocation per virtual CPU. The instance does not include integrated local disk storage, depending entirely on network block storage volumes for persistent data operations, and contains zero discrete GPU accelerators. Networking provisions include a single complimentary public IPv4 address. With a high ratio of RAM relative to dedicated execution cores, this server configuration provides dependable computational throughput for memory-intensive workloads, including in-memory databases, continuous integration build clusters, search indices, and large enterprise application runtimes requiring substantial resident execution memory without dedicated accelerator hardware.
